ai.description: This slender, worm-like snake reaches 20–30 cm. It is uniform brown or grey with a pale snout and tail tip. Key features include 14 scale rows around the body and a rounded, non-distinct head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Myriopholis blanfordii* is best distinguished by its single preocular scale, which separates it from similar species that typically possess two preoculars.
ai.habitat: *Myriopholis blanfordii* inhabits arid and semi-arid regions, typically found in sandy soils, scrublands, and rocky foothills at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Sindh thread snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time burrowing through loose soil in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Myriopholis blanfordii* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 3–5 elongated eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between July and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Myriopholis blanfordii* occurs in the arid regions of northwestern India, specifically in Rajasthan and Gujarat, ranging from lowlands up to moderate elevations.
